messages.author: 7d8868e81d2b7b64
messages.subject: qtl model question for Non-normal phenotypes
parts:
Dear Karl Broman,

My data show non-normal distribution,  Shapiro-wilk test w =0.89,p-value <1.2E-08.

The question is: For this data, Can i use stepwise with 'normal' model?  
1. In the paper https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/29375602 , they have the samiler phenotype distribution as my, they do Shapiro-wilk test p-value < 1.1E - 08,
the data also was not notmally distributed, but they use the model scanone(normal),scantwo and stepwise(normal). This made me very confused.

2. I tried many models like scanone(normal, binary, 2part, np), CIM, scantwo, stepwise(normal, binary). 
 --> For Scanone, i got two QTLs. one is very strong on chr3, other one is on chr4 just over significance threshold. In addition, there are two peaks close to the threshold, located at chr1 and chr 7 respectively.
 --> Comparing results of 'normal' and  'np',  ‘np’ is obviously more suitable than ‘normal’ for my data ( 'np' got much higher LOD and more easier to expain the relationship between qtl and variables)
 --> For the scantwo, alphas=c(0.05,0.05,0,0.05,0.05), there were no pairs of loci meeting the criteria.
 --> For stepwise,  I don't understand how many max.qtl i should use. I tried 'normal' model wirth max.qtl = 10, 8 ,  5, 4 respectively.
        Use the 'imp'  method:
             ->when max.qtl = 10 and 8,  2 ~ 8 QTLs are detected in different variables. New qtls were detected on chr 2 and 6; There is no correlation between qtls and variables, and 2~3 qtls are detected on each unexpected chromsome.
                This result looks strange, but used 'fitqtl' to detect the models,  I got very high pLOD and %var.
For example:.
           -> When max.qtl =  5, 1~5 QTLs are detected in different variables ,  on chr1, chr3, chr4, chr6, chr7; 
For example:
             ->  When max.qtl =  4 , 1 QTL on chr3  or chr4  was detected.

For example:
       
I am really confused about which results is more confidence and Can i use stepwise with 'normal' model? Do you have any good suggestions about this?

Thank you for you help

Have a good day.

Ningning

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] qtl model question for Non-normal phenotypes
parts:
I'm not sure how best to treat this phenotype, but I'd be inclined to separate the spike at 0 from the rest. The issue of how to do the QTL mapping is equivalent to how to handle this phenotype when doing multiple regression.

I'd study carefully what's going on with the tightly linked QTL, particularly the pair on chromosome A6. I expect that they are likely an artifact.

karl
